item.title: SuperCmd Beta 2.0.0-beta
item.description:
SuperCmd Beta 2.0.0-beta

The first beta of SuperCmd 2.0. It installs as SuperCmd Beta next to the stable app, with its own settings, clipboard and notes database, extensions, file index and update feed, so your stable install stays untouched. Everything merged since 1.0.9 is in this build. Run one channel at a time for global hotkeys, the Hyper Key and browser sign-in. Apple silicon only, like the stable app.

New Features

Window Switcher

  • Tiles are ordered by the window you used most recently, so one tap of the hotkey goes back to the window you just left, even a full-screen window on another Space. Windows you have never focused follow in the system's order.
  • ⌘Tab and ⌘⇧Tab can now be recorded as the switcher's hotkey. SuperCmd releases the system app switcher's chord while it holds it and hands it back on quit, and after a crash, so the system switcher is never left dead.
  • Previews are kept between opens, so the grid paints with real thumbnails the moment it appears instead of trickling in over app icons. The cache is bounded at 16 MiB.
  • Each tile shows the owning app's icon in the bottom-right corner of the preview. The selected tile has a near-white border and a lifted card instead of the accent blue that vanished over blue windows.
  • The grid is sized for the screen it opens on, so a second monitor with a different width no longer gets a grid wider than the panel. Closing windows from inside the switcher (X, ⌫, ⌘W) shrinks the panel to fit.
  • Opening from an empty Desktop, or after clicking the desktop, selects the window you just left instead of skipping past it.
  • Browser tab hover cards, hidden title strips and other helper windows no longer appear as tiles with Show windows from all Desktops on.
  • The switcher draws on the same backdrop as the launcher and follows Window Style, Background Tint and Transparency, with more room around the grid and properly rounded corners.
  • Closing a window from the switcher no longer lags.

Appearance

  • Settings → General → Appearance → Window Style chooses between Frosted, the existing blur, and Liquid Glass, the native macOS 26 material drawn the way Spotlight draws its panel. The picker appears on macOS 26 and later. Frosted stays the default.
  • A Transparency slider for Liquid Glass fades from the regular material to a clear one with the wallpaper showing through, keeping the refraction at every setting.
  • Background Tint now applies to both styles, and each style remembers its own value.
  • The bottom islands (the ⌘ circle, the mode label, the hint pill, the Open ↩ / Actions ⌘K capsule and the note window's formatting bar), the ⌘K menu and the widget tiles draw on the shared glass, so they follow the chosen style and tint instead of staying frosted.
  • Light mode rendering fixes for Liquid Glass.
  • Settings → General → Appearance → Font renders the launcher in any installed font family, or System Default. The choice is per Mac and not synced. Families that ship only Regular and Bold, such as Menlo, no longer render the whole panel bold.
  • Widget tiles are lighter cards with a soft hairline, the stray divider under the widget strip is gone, and the results fade ends at the panel's true bottom edge under a two-row widget strip.
  • Reset Launcher Position centers the panel exactly between the menu bar and the Dock instead of 80 pt above center.

Screenshots

  • Settings → Screenshots → Screenshot Folder is now the history's content: every image in the folder appears, newest first, up to 300, including captures macOS saved there with ⇧⌘3 and ⇧⌘4. Imported images are searchable by their text and open in the annotation editor.
  • SuperCmd never writes, moves or deletes an image it did not create. Deleting an imported row leaves the file in place and keeps it from being imported again. A file that leaves the folder takes its row with it.
  • ↩ and a double-click preview a screenshot in the system Quick Look panel instead of an in-panel overlay. ⌘Y opens it from the ⌘K menu, like image clips and file rows.
  • Reveal in Finder reveals the real file when a row has one.

Extensions

  • Update Extension re-downloads an installed extension in place, from the Extension Store ⌘K menu, the launcher's ⌘K menu on an extension command, and a ↻ button in Settings → Extensions. Preferences, aliases, pins, hotkeys, menu-bar items and sign-ins survive, and a running menu-bar item relaunches on the new bundle.
  • Store: Check for Updates compares the published bundle's time rather than the catalog row, so an extension no longer shows as updatable every time someone else installs it. The Store detail page's Last update reads the same time.
  • Typing an extension or script command's alias and pressing Space enters its argument fill, the way it already did for a quicklink.
  • ↩ on an extension command with arguments puts the caret in the first empty pill. A second ↩ runs it unless a required pill is still empty. The highlight no longer jumps to the next row, the typed query stays, and commands with required arguments get a caret.
  • QR Code Scanner works again: codes that use legacy text encodings decode, and the command returns to the launcher when it finishes instead of leaving a blank screen.

Script Commands

  • Script Commands can carry a launcher alias. Each row in Settings → Scripts has the same alias pill as Applications, Commands, Quicklinks and Extensions.

Dictation

  • Settings → Dictation → Behavior → Output chooses where the transcript goes: Paste to active app (the default), Copy to clipboard, or Paste and copy. Copying shows a Copied to clipboard toast.
  • A chime plays when the microphone goes live and again when the session ends. Pick None, Bubble (the default), Octave or Marimba under Settings → Dictation → Behavior → Sound.
  • The hold-to-talk key can be any of F1 to F17 or a left-side ⌘, ⌥, ⌃ or ⇧, in addition to Fn and the right-side modifiers. A held function key is swallowed so it never reaches the app you are dictating into.

Search Files

  • Settings → File Search → Index Source → Use Spotlight Index builds the file index from Spotlight instead of a folder scan. Index Stats shows which source is in use. The setting is per Mac.
  • Rows show the bare file name. The folder path returns only when two results share a name.
  • Open With… in the ⌘K menu is a nested list of apps: the default handler first, every app registered for the file with its icon, and Other… for the Open panel.
  • Share… in the ⌘K menu lists the system share services, such as AirDrop, Messages and Notes, for files in Search Files, the launcher's file rows and Clipboard History.

Clipboard History

  • A copied file is previewed in the detail pane: a thumbnail for images, PDFs and movies, the text for text files, the file icon otherwise, with the name and folder underneath. ⌘Y opens it in Quick Look.
  • Pasting or copying an entry moves it to the top of the history without adding a duplicate. Pinned entries stay where they are.

Quicklinks

  • A quicklink whose link is a file path can be dragged out of the panel as a file, from its launcher row and from Search Quicklinks.
  • Typing a quicklink's alias and pressing Space puts the caret in its first argument pill. Space never opens the link.
  • New Quicklink and the pencil button in Settings → Quicklinks open the in-panel editor, the same one Create Quicklink uses.

Notes

  • Show/Hide Notes is a new command that hides every floating note window or brings them back. With no note window open it opens the most recently edited note. It gets a hotkey row in Settings → Notes.
  • The note window has a resize grip in the bottom-right corner, text dissolves under the title bar as it scrolls instead of being cut off, the scroller sits flush with the window's edge, and the first line starts just under the title bar.
  • The scroll bar is always the thin overlay style, even with a mouse attached or Show scroll bars set to Always. The hover highlight on the formatting bar's end controls follows the capsule's curve.

Snippets

  • Settings → Snippets is a new pane with an Enable Snippets switch, an expansion sound (None or any of the fourteen macOS alert sounds) and hotkey rows for Search Snippets and Create Snippet.

Launcher

  • Escape Key Behavior in Settings → Launcher decides what a bare Escape does. Navigate back or close window, the new default, steps back one level per press, the way ⌫ in an empty field does, and closes only from the root. Close window and pop to root keeps the previous one-press behavior.
  • Escape Key Closes Window decides whether Escape closes the Settings window, the AI Chat window and the note windows.
  • The search bar floats over every mode, not just the launcher, and content dissolves under it as it scrolls.
  • The ⌘K actions menu can open nested levels in place: ↩ or → enters, ← or ⌫ on an empty filter returns, and Escape steps out one level per press.
  • Define Word suggests the nearest words for a misspelling: "recieve" offers "receive", with ↑ ↓ to choose and ↩ to look up.
  • The calculator names currencies in a conversion: "1 usd to inr" shows US Dollar and Indian Rupee under the expression and the result.
  • The compact launcher grows in the same frame as the first keystroke, with no flash of the full chrome inside the collapsed bar.
  • The Memory widget matches Activity Monitor's Memory Used.
  • The Uninstaller opens instantly and finds related files in the background. Items you cannot move yourself, such as a root-owned App Store app, are moved to the Trash after an administrator prompt (Touch ID or password) instead of failing. Rows that need it carry a lock badge.

Color Picker

  • The eyedropper reads the exact color on screen. It converted through the wrong color profile before, so a mid grey came back lighter and a red shifted toward orange, and on Retina displays each loupe cell blended four pixels.
  • The loupe works on every display, with one overlay per screen.

Improvements

  • Dead-key and IME compositions survive in the search field. Typing an accent slowly on a dead-key layout, or a Pinyin or Japanese candidate, is no longer dropped while the launcher re-renders.
  • When a ⌘K menu closes, the caret returns to the search field in every mode.
  • Lists in the panel never show the thick legacy scroll bar when Show scroll bars is set to Always.
  • The launcher's notes preview scrolls to the bottom edge and fades under the action bar instead of ending in a hard clip.
  • The launcher is dragged by its header. The body no longer moves the window, so selecting text or clicking between rows never drags it. Dropping near the screen's center snaps the panel onto the guide after release, with no jitter during the drag.
  • Translate: the arrow between the panes is a plain hint rather than a button, and the input editor hides its scroll bar.
  • Settings sidebar icons fit their tiles whatever the symbol's shape.
  • Grok chat no longer breaks when the service raises its minimum client version. SuperCmd adopts the new floor and retries, so it recovers on the next message without an update.

Bug Fixes

  • Fixed the 1.0.9 crash on Macs that never loaded a local AI model. The GPU cache was cleared before any model existed, which could fault under memory pressure or when toggling an AI feature.
  • App discovery no longer re-runs every 2 to 64 seconds for the life of the process because of a system bundle without an Info.plist. Idle memory on an affected Mac dropped from about 295 MB to about 91 MB.
  • The window switcher no longer ranks a window left before a disable and re-enable above everything used since.

item.title: SuperCmd Beta 1.0.8-beta
item.description:
First separate SuperCmd Beta build, version 1.0.8-beta (1).
- Installs as SuperCmd Beta with a separate app identifier. - Keeps local preferences, history, and extension data separate from the stable app. - Uses an independent beta update feed; stable users remain on the stable channel.
Requires macOS 15 or later and Apple silicon.
Run one channel at a time for global hotkeys and browser sign-in. Account credentials and the supercmd:// callback scheme remain shared with stable.
